title: A fresh reply allows imperfect courage

captions.physics: Discovering a compulsory script lacks confirmation
captions.energy: Opening a reply without a script
captions.emotions: Feeling gentle courage in your words

meaning: You can discover that a compulsory prepared remark lacks confirmation and open the possibility of an unscripted reply, feeling gentle courage to speak in your own words.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Tower in the physical position reveals that a supposedly compulsory prepared remark was not confirmed. The Fool in energy supports openness to an unscripted answer and a beginning with words still unknown. Strength in emotions brings gentle courage and tolerance of awkwardness. You can discover a proposed example was never a requirement. A fresh beginning does not oblige immediate fluency: another reply can be attempted with doubt or a wish to clarify the question.

For example, a suggested greeting is discussed as imposed words “from both of us” until it becomes clear that it was only an example. The earlier accusation loses its basis. **Words of your own can begin awkwardly**. You can explain what does not fit and leave another version unfinished. Courage emerges to answer without having to defend someone else’s wording. Yet the example does not become forbidden: it can be accepted freely, changed or replaced by a different remark altogether.

Difficulty arises if freedom to answer becomes a demand for immediate improvisation. Asking for time or a suitable example then seems insufficiently brave. The constructive Fool helps leave the beginning genuinely open, including words not yet found. You can feel courage and still request clarification; independence is not measured by speed, while gentleness towards awkwardness allows familiar wording where both choose it without any obligation to perform novelty.
